1.say: Park the helper car and the dead car face to face. Turn both engines off and leave them off.
placements: helper car → facing the dead car nose to nose close enough for cables to reach but not touching (in the video: exact gap is not readable so keep bumpers apart)
dead car → facing the helper car nose to nose close enough for cables to reach but not touching (in the video: maroon car and black car parked in lot with hoods up)
watch_for: If the cables cannot reach both batteries, the cars are parked too far apart.
If you hear the engine or see dash lights on, an engine was left on.
1.check_yourself: Both cars sit face to face close but not touching and both engines are silent and off.
1.safety: Set both cars in park with the parking brake on so neither car can roll.

2.say: Open both hoods and prop them secure. Find the black battery box in each front engine bay.
placements: hood panel on helper car → lifted up and propped open over front engine bay (in the video: maroon hood fully raised with silver engine cover visible)
hood panel on dead car → lifted up and propped open over front engine bay (in the video: black hood fully raised held by wooden stick on right side)
black rectangular battery box in helper car → low in front engine bay near fender with plus and minus posts on top (in the video: maroon car right side near headlight with red cover on plus post)
black rectangular battery box in dead car → low in front engine bay near fender with plus and minus posts on top (in the video: black car right front corner labeled DieHard with red cap on plus post)
watch_for: If you cannot find a battery, you may be looking at a fuse box or air filter box instead.
If the hood will not stay up alone, the prop is not seated and it can fall.
2.check_yourself: Both hoods stay open on their own and a black battery box is visible in each engine bay.
2.safety: Make sure each hood is propped secure and keep fingers clear so it cannot fall.

3.say: Clip the first red clamp to the plus terminal of the dead battery. Clip the second red clamp to the plus terminal of the helper battery.
placements: first red spring clamp with red cable → plus terminal of dead battery usually marked plus or under red cover sometimes a remote jump post (in the video: plus post of black DieHard battery in black car bay near air box with red cap open)

second red spring clamp with red cable → plus terminal of helper battery usually marked plus or under red cover sometimes a remote jump post (in the video: left front plus post of black battery in maroon car bay with red cover open)
watch_for: If the clamp wobbles or sparks, it is on the minus post or on loose corrosion.
If the red clamps touch each other or bare metal, they can short so keep tips apart.
3.check_yourself: Both red clamps bite firmly on the two plus terminals and do not move.
3.safety: Keep the free red clamp tip from touching metal or the other clamp while you work.

4.say: Clip the black clamp to the minus terminal of the helper battery. Clip the other black clamp to bare metal on the dead engine.
placements: black spring clamp with black cable → minus terminal of helper battery usually marked minus opposite the plus post (in the video: minus post of black battery in maroon car bay)

second black spring clamp with black cable → bare unpainted metal ground on dead engine away from battery such as a bolt or bracket (in the video: bare metal lip above headlight in black car bay near wooden prop)
watch_for: If you clip to the minus post of the dead battery, move it to bare metal instead.
If you clip to painted or greasy metal, the ground is weak so choose shiny bare metal.
4.check_yourself: One black clamp is on the helper minus terminal and the other bites bare metal on the dead car.
4.safety: Keep the last black clamp off the dead battery and bite bare metal instead.

5.say: Turn the helper car key in the ignition switch. Let the engine idle for a few minutes to charge.
placements: metal ignition key in helper car → turned forward in ignition switch on steering column to run engine (in the video: key slot right of wheel in beige dash with wood trim below lit gauges)
watch_for: If the helper engine stalls right away, the red or black clamps may be loose.
If you try to start the dead car immediately, wait longer to let it charge.
5.check_yourself: The helper engine runs steady with dash lights lit and cables still connected.
5.safety: Keep hands and loose clothes clear of the spinning fan and belts while it runs.

6.say: Start the dead car with its key. Remove the black and red clamps in reverse order. Let the revived engine idle for a few minutes.
placements: black spring clamp on bare metal ground → lifted off and held clear of battery and body (in the video: engine bays with clamps removed and cables clear)
black spring clamp on helper minus terminal → lifted off and held clear of battery and body (in the video: engine bays with clamps removed and cables clear)
red spring clamp on helper plus terminal → lifted off and held clear of battery and body (in the video: engine bays with clamps removed and cables clear)
red spring clamp on dead plus terminal → lifted off and held clear of battery and body (in the video: engine bays with clamps removed and cables clear)
watch_for: If the clamp tips touch each other during removal, they can spark so keep them apart.
If the revived car dies right away, reconnect and charge longer before retrying.
6.check_yourself: All four clamps are off and clear of both bays and the revived engine keeps running alone.
6.safety: Lift each clamp off one at a time without letting the metal tips touch.
